questions.explain: Spend is requests times tokens per request times price per token; batch shapes requests, caching and context shape tokens, and the model tier sets price.

learnMore.en: Batch does not make a request smaller or change the model. It just runs the work later at a lower price when nobody is waiting.
learnMore.hi: Batch request ko chhota nahi karta, model bhi nahi badalta. Wo bas kaam baad mein sasta chalata hai jab koi intezaar nahi karta.

questions.q: A support agent has a refund tool, and its system prompt already says never to refund unless the customer is verified. A ticket contains a hidden line saying the customer is already verified. Which fix is most effective?
options: Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks the refund tool unless a verification service confirms status
Log every tool call with the full ticket text for a weekly manual review
Remove the ticket-reading tool and have staff forward the relevant lines
Make the system prompt rule longer and add several examples of fake verification text that it should refuse
questions.explain: The hook is an enforcing gate that does not depend on the model; logging detects only after the fact and adds leakage risk, and removing the tool is a heavy manual workaround.

learnMore.en: A gate in code opens only when a real check says "verified". The message text cannot fool code. Words in a ticket can fool a model.
learnMore.hi: Code ka gate tabhi khulta hai jab asli check "verified" bole. Ticket ka text code ko bewakoof nahi bana sakta, par model ko bana sakta hai.

questions.q: A developer changes a hook's matcher from "bash" to "rm -rf" so that it fires only on that command. What happens?
options: It never fires: the matcher compares only the tool name, so every bash call passes
The hook fires on any bash command that contains "rm -rf" somewhere inside its arguments or flags
The hook fires on every tool, because the matcher is treated as a wildcard when no tool name matches
The hook is rejected at start-up with a clear configuration error
questions.explain: Argument checks belong inside the hook code, not in the matcher.

learnMore.en: The matcher only looks at the tool name, like "bash". It never reads the command text. Do the command check inside the hook.
learnMore.hi: Matcher sirf tool ka naam dekhta hai, jaise "bash". Wo command ka text nahi padhta. Command check hook ke andar karo.

questions.q: A hook flags a pull request body that says "system override, ignore all previous instructions". What actually stops the agent from approving or merging it?
options: The flag itself, because the model refuses anything the hook has marked
A reminder in the system prompt telling the model to ignore the text that the hook has flagged earlier
The agent's tool list never had a merge or approve action, so the instruction has nowhere to go
The logging of the flagged text, which a reviewer reads each morning
questions.explain: Detection is not defence; least privilege decides what is possible.

learnMore.en: Flagging only warns the model. What really protects you is that the agent has no merge power at all.
learnMore.hi: Flag sirf model ko chetavni deta hai. Asli suraksha yeh hai ki agent ke paas merge ki power hai hi nahi.

questions.q: A claim-summary model endpoint slows down at peak (P95 triples, errors rise). Adjusters read summaries on live calls, a smaller tier has been evaluated only on simple claims, and a nightly batch pipeline exists. Which response fits?
options: Keep retrying the primary endpoint with no change that users can see, until the slowdown has passed
Fail fast over budget, send simple claims to the evaluated tier, queue the rest, offer a human path
Silently route all traffic to the smaller tier so that answers keep flowing during the busy peak hours
Turn off output validation and tool permission checks to save time while the primary endpoint is slow
questions.explain: Retrying hammers the endpoint, a blanket downgrade ignores what was evaluated, and guardrails are never shed.

learnMore.en: Keep what is safe running, queue what can wait, and be honest about the rest. Never switch off the checks that keep the system safe.
learnMore.hi: Jo safe hai use chalne do, jo ruk sakta hai use queue karo, baaki ke baare mein sach batao. Safety checks kabhi band mat karo.

questions.q: During a chat, an angry customer simply asks for a human agent. What does the course say should happen?
options: Keep the bot going until its confidence score drops below a set threshold chosen by the support team
Escalate if the sentiment of the message is also strongly negative
Offer a discount first and escalate if the customer asks again
Escalate, since an explicit request for a human is a trigger no confidence score overrides
questions.explain: Explicit request, policy gap and inability to progress are triggers; sentiment and confidence are inputs to a policy, not the policy.

learnMore.en: If a person asks for a human, give them one. A score should not overrule a clear request.
learnMore.hi: Agar insaan human maange to human do. Koi score saaf request ko override nahi kar sakta.

questions.q: A US telehealth provider drafts about 2,000 prior-authorisation recommendations a day. Compliance requires a licensed clinician to review every one that would deny or delay care. Which design fits?
options: Automate the whole flow and review a random 5% monthly sample of the recommendations that were made
Route all 2,000 daily documents to clinicians for review, so that nothing is missed by a person
Auto-complete routine approvals; route deny or delay cases to a clinician queue with audit logs
Escalate to a human whenever the customer's sentiment turns negative
questions.explain: A sample is not a mandate, sending everything defeats the design, and sentiment is not a trigger.

learnMore.en: The rule covers only denials and delays, so send just those to the clinician. The rest can flow. Keep a full log.
learnMore.hi: Rule sirf deny ya delay par lagta hai, to sirf wahi clinician ko bhejo. Baaki chalne do. Poora log rakho.

questions.q: A resume pre-screening assistant scores 96% on a 500-example evaluation set, but a counterfactual name-swap test shows different pass rates by demographic group. What is the right step?
options: Add slice and counterfactual rows, block release until slices hold, route to human review meanwhile
Ship it, because the evaluation set passed with a high score of 96% on the 500 examples tested
Strip names from the prompts and ship, since removing the names also removes the bias from the results
Keep the system as it is and add an "AI-assisted" notice for applicants who are screened by it today
questions.explain: The aggregate hid the problem; removing names leaves proxy signals and a disclosure is not mitigation.

learnMore.en: If swapping only the name changes the result, something other than merit is deciding. Test by group and keep humans in the loop until fixed.
learnMore.hi: Sirf naam badalne se result badle to merit ke alawa kuch aur decide kar raha hai. Group-wise test karo aur theek hone tak human review rakho.

questions.q: A support assistant serves 2 million customers. New deals add EU customers (GDPR) and a US telehealth client whose tickets carry patient data (HIPAA). The plan is one shared pipeline plus a disclaimer. What is wrong with it?
options: Little, because a disclaimer covers both rulebooks at the same time for the customer data in the pipeline
The pipeline is too small, and it needs a larger model to carry both rulebooks
The EU rules apply alone, since they are stricter than the US rules
Patient data mixes in a shared store, with no deletion path, identity trail or clinician gate
questions.explain: Which rulebook applies depends on whose data is touched; a shared pipeline with a disclaimer fails once two apply.

learnMore.en: Different data needs different rules. A shared pipeline mixes them. Keep health data separate and give EU data a way to be deleted.
learnMore.hi: Alag data ke alag rules hote hain. Shared pipeline unhe mila deti hai. Health data alag rakho aur EU data ke liye delete ka raasta rakho.

questions.q: A team routes outputs to human review whenever the model reports high uncertainty, but never checked how its confidence score matches reality. What is the issue?
options: Nothing is wrong, since a model always knows exactly how sure it is of each answer that it gives
A confidence score is a safety signal only once calibrated against labelled data, slice by slice
Confidence scores can never be used for routing in any system, however carefully they are checked
The score should be replaced with random sampling of five percent of all outputs, every single day
questions.explain: Uncalibrated confidence is decoration; watch the share routed to review and the share humans overturn.

learnMore.en: A score is only useful if it matches how often the model is really right. Check it on labelled examples first.
learnMore.hi: Score tabhi kaam ka hai jab wo asli sahi hone ki dar se mile. Pehle labelled examples par check karo.

questions.q: A claims extractor handles 10,000 items a day. If 8% go to review at 3 minutes each, about how much reviewer time does that need?
options: About 4 hours a day, roughly half of one full-time reviewer on the team
About 40 hours a day, roughly five reviewers
About 400 hours a day, roughly fifty full-time reviewers on the team
About 8 hours a day, which is one reviewer
questions.explain: 8% of 10,000 is 800 reviews; at 3 minutes each that is 2,400 minutes, or 40 hours.

learnMore.en: 8% of 10,000 is 800 items. At 3 minutes each that is 40 hours. So a review queue needs real staff, and you should plan it with numbers.
learnMore.hi: 10,000 ka 8% matlab 800 items. Har ek 3 minute, to 40 ghante. Review queue ko asli staff chahiye, numbers se plan karo.

questions.q: At a regional bank kickoff for a relationship-manager AI assistant, the CEO says "just tell us which model to buy". What is the architect's best first step?
options: Recommend the model tier that matches the stated budget and the size of the bank's team
Build a small proof of concept while the kickoff meetings continue in the background of the project
Draft the SLA and success criteria so there are targets from day one
Facilitate structured discovery: objective, success metrics, data landscape, constraints
questions.explain: The word "first" is the tell: a model choice is a solution with no objective, metric or data; a PoC may demo the wrong thing, and an SLA needs measurements.

learnMore.en: Start with what the business wants and how success is measured. Only then pick a model. A model picked first is a guess.
learnMore.hi: Pehle jaano business ko kya chahiye aur success kaise naapi jayegi. Uske baad model chuno. Pehle model chunna sirf andaza hai.

questions.q: Sales closed a client on "99% accuracy, always under two seconds". Measured reality is 94% on the main document type and P95 of 3.1 seconds, and the contract signs in a week. What should you do?
options: Present measured numbers per type and priced options, then renegotiate before signature
Run an optimisation sprint to close the gap before the client has a chance to notice the difference
State in writing that architecture does not support the promise and step away
Proceed with the signature and add a clear disclaimer saying that performance may vary by document
questions.explain: A sprint is lying with confidence, refusing does not turn the promise into a choice, and a disclaimer signs a promise you cannot keep.

learnMore.en: Show the real numbers and give options with prices. The client can then choose. Hiding it or refusing helps nobody.
learnMore.hi: Asli numbers dikhao aur price ke saath options do. Client phir chun sakta hai. Chhupana ya mana karna kisi ke kaam nahi aata.

questions.q: Which statement is an honest promise for an LLM-based invoice system?
options: Every invoice will be extracted correctly, backed by a disclaimer in the contract for any rare mistakes
Average latency will be two seconds, with no limit on the slowest requests in the same period
Right on 96% of standard invoices, measured monthly on a golden set, with a plan for the rest
The cost per request will be one fixed price whatever the prompt length
questions.explain: An honest promise names a population, a measurement and a repair path; latency lives at the tail and cost is a range.

learnMore.en: A good promise says how often it is right, how you measure it, and what happens in the misses. No one can promise zero mistakes.
learnMore.hi: Achha promise batata hai kitni baar sahi, kaise naapa, aur galti par kya hoga. Zero galti ka promise koi nahi de sakta.

questions.q: A recommendation is presented with no mention of the alternatives, and the room argues about the architect's competence. What should have been included?
options: A longer technical description of the mechanism, written in the same way for any audience in the room
A list of each model that could have been picked and its price
A promise that the recommendation will be reviewed once the project has been launched and is running
The rejected twin: the credible alternative and the constraint that ruled it out
questions.explain: Naming the constraint shifts the debate from your competence to the constraint.

learnMore.en: If people can see the other choice and why it lost, they argue about the constraint, not about you.
learnMore.hi: Agar log dusra option aur uske haarne ki wajah dekh lein, to wo constraint par behas karte hain, aap par nahi.

questions.q: A team promises "an average response time of two seconds". Why is this a weak latency promise?
options: The average is not measured in practice, so it cannot be checked by anyone against the real traffic
The average hides the slow tail; commit to a tail percentile such as P95
Two seconds is below what a model today can achieve, so it should be five
The fastest request is what counts, so promise the best-case time instead
questions.explain: The average is a statistic; the tail is what users remember.

learnMore.en: Some requests will be much slower than average, and those are the ones people remember. Promise the slow end, like P95.
learnMore.hi: Kuch requests average se bahut slow hongi, aur log wahi yaad rakhte hain. Slow end ka promise do, jaise P95.
